definition: Resolute means firm and determined; refusing to waver.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word resolute. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know resolute should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Three hours of cross-examination could not shake the witness; she remained resolute, repeating her account without changing a single detail.
Determined says you truly intend to do it; resolute goes further - the decision is settled, and pressure will not reopen it.
Immovable outdoes resolute: the resolute negotiator holds her position through every argument, while an immovable one will not even return to the table to hear a new offer.

Steadfast praises loyalty that holds steady over time — the friend still beside you in year ten, the ally who never drifts. Resolute points at one decision: the mind is made up, and pressure will not reopen it. Steadfast is proven across years; resolute is proven the moment pressure arrives.

Unwavering describes the visible surface of firmness — no flicker, no hesitation, nothing bending at any point. Resolute names what sits underneath: a decision already made and closed to argument. A rehearsed voice can sound unwavering; only someone who has genuinely settled the choice is resolute.

Firm is the everyday, all-purpose word for holding a position — a firm offer, a firm handshake, a firm no. Resolute is stronger and more admiring: the decision is settled and will not bend under real pressure. A firm answer holds for now; a resolute one has closed the question.

Imani Sesay moved the marsh orchid into a different genus, half the botanical world objected within a month.
Journal editors hinted at retraction, conference panels were arranged to rebut her, and a senior rival wrote three open letters.
Sesay stayed resolute: she had spent nine seasons in the field before deciding, and she declined to reopen the question under pressure.
Asked whether anything could change her mind, she answered that a new specimen could - a louder letter could not.
Two independent genetic studies later confirmed the reclassification, and the letters quietly stopped.
